html:
Ardashir I was the founder of the Sasanian Empire, the last great Iranian empire before Islam. A local king in Fars, the old Persian homeland in southern Iran, he rose against the Parthian king.

In 224 he defeated and killed the Parthian king Artabanus IV at the battle of Hormozdgan and took the title of King of Kings of Iran. He built round cities such as Ardashir-Khwarrah, today's Firuzabad, and carved his triumphs on rock reliefs near Persepolis.

He fought Rome over Mesopotamia and made Zoroastrianism the backbone of royal power. His son Shapur I, who captured the Roman emperor Valerian, built on his work. The empire lasted until the Arab conquests of the 630s and 640s.
